sampling_model.design: The identification kernel compares full positive-definite covariance images of centred linear Gaussian SEMs; the statistical rung uses independent Gaussian sampling and global BIC over the finite labelled state class.
sampling_model.units: Each observation is one independent realization of the \(p\)-variable system with known zero mean.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment in the structure-identification kernel; ordered pairs in \(\mathcal Q\) index downstream interventions and responses.
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; every innovation variance is positive and otherwise unrestricted.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Target-local block-incidence regressions estimate one coefficient per parent block and one residual variance per target. The effect maps use the same constrained regressions before finite path summation. The inferential claims are fixed in \(p\), pointwise outside \(\mathcal E_C\), and conditional on global rather than greedy optimization.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 19 proves structural identifiability within BPEC-DAGs, whose edge-colour classes all have size at least two, and Question 20 asks for a graphical characterization of edge-coloured model equivalence.
Theorem 2 transforms equivalent DAGs through exactly their distinct disagreeing edges, each reversed while covered.
Theorem 2.17 characterizes generic covariance-submatrix rank by trek separation and determinant expansions.
The paper explains classes of nested covariance constraints through restricted trek separation but gives no uniform arithmetic-height witness for coefficient-coloured model inequivalence.
Theorem 4.1 characterizes partial-homoscedastic model equivalence by ordinary Markov equivalence and fixed parent sets for vertices in nonsingleton variance blocks.
Theorem 4.4 characterizes existence and uniqueness of the MLE in a fixed compatibly coloured RDAG by linear independence of augmented sample vectors.
The paper gives linear-delay enumeration of ordinary Markov-equivalent DAGs and consistent extensions under background knowledge.
The paper extends Schwarz-type model-selection asymptotics to a finite collection of smoothly curved submodels of an exponential family.
The paper derives asymptotic inference for graph-indexed joint-intervention effects over an ordinary estimated Markov-equivalence class.
The paper constructs test-inversion confidence regions for total effects under equal error variances while accounting for structural uncertainty.

body.tldr: Target-local equality constraints among structural coefficients encode causal communities, but permitting singleton communities restores observational ambiguity. Every discrepancy detected by the proved signature criterion is nevertheless exposed by a unit-noise covariance generated from at most two coefficient-one blocks at one target, with integer entries bounded by \(p\) and an exact determinant or cleared-regression value in \(\{-2,-1,1,2\}\). The resulting universal binary-star library has the exact size \(\sum_j[|\Pi^{E_0}_j|+\binom{|\Pi^{E_0}_j|}{2}]\), at most the sharp worst-case value \(\binom{p+1}{3}\). Covariance-model equality is equivalent to signature equality and to connectivity by legal singleton covered reversals, enabling exact component enumeration and a qualified fixed-\(p\) rung for generic global-BIC component recovery and simultaneous member-labelled total-effect inference.

project_justification.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 proves identifiability only when every blocked edge-colour class is nonsingleton and leaves graphical equivalence open. Its rational constraints and the determinant machinery of SullivantTalaskaDraisma2010 and DrtonRobevaWeihs2020 do not provide a uniformly small observable witness, an exactly counted universal witness library, or a sharp worst-case library bound when singleton blocks are admitted.
project_justification.niche: The target-local blocked class has enough structure for every skeleton, collider, block-family, or unequal-family orientation mismatch to be routed to one sparse star calculation. Partition disjointness makes the star parametrization injective, while acyclicity bounds the exact library size through a topological order, and the class still contains ordinary Markov equivalence and the proper BPEC boundary as opposite special cases.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the four-case binary-star router and logarithmic numerical-height guarantee, counts its universal library exactly and obtains the sharp bound \(\binom{p+1}{3}\), lifts Chickering's disagreement-decreasing sequence to the exact legal blocked move graph, enumerates the resulting component, and establishes pointwise generic selection and effect-set inference without claiming uniformity at model intersections.

body.related_work: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 provides the model exemplar: its Introduction moves from equality-constrained causal coefficients to causal communities, Theorem 19 proves proper BPEC identifiability, and Question 20 isolates general edge-coloured equivalence; the present strict advance is confined to target-local blocked colours with singleton blocks and adds bounded constructive separators together with an exactly counted binary-star dictionary whose sharp worst-case size is \(\binom{p+1}{3}\). Chickering1995, Theorems 1 and 2, supplies the ordinary skeleton-collider criterion and the disagreement-decreasing covered-reversal induction; the new step is proving that equal blocked signatures force every selected move to be singleton and partition-compatible. SullivantTalaskaDraisma2010 supplies the determinant-expansion viewpoint, while DrtonRobevaWeihs2020 supplies the cleared rational-constraint analogue; both inform the certificate proof but are not claimed to be sharpened in their general graph classes. WuDrton2023 gives the nearest complete partition-restricted equivalence theorem for innovation variances, a different parameter restriction. MakamReichenbachSeigal2023 supplies the target-local pooled-regression likelihood construction. WienobstLuttermannBannachLiskiewicz2023 informs consistent-extension enumeration with background arrows. Haughton1988 informs the smooth finite-model BIC argument. NandyMaathuisRichardson2017 and StriederDrton2023 inform the simultaneous effect-set inference rung. Targeted searches through September 2026 found no paper occupying the bounded binary-star target-method pair, the exact sharp dictionary count, or the stated singleton-permitting blocked equivalence criterion.
body.interpretation: The causal target is the covariance-model equivalence component, whereas the proved signature criterion and finite star dictionary are observable-law recovery devices. A signature mismatch can be rejected by searching a finite source-model library, and the exact count shows the computational certificate budget is determined by the parent-block counts. The sharp worst case occurs for a complete acyclic graph with singleton parent blocks; coarser blocks or missing arrows can only reduce the library.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Exact-arithmetic enumeration through \(p=5\) remains a diagnostic audit of the constructive proof, not a premise of it: the all-\(p\) router, exact dictionary count, and sharp bound are established symbolically. The unresolved certificate Pareto question is whether a different universal scheme can improve on two active blocks or height \(\lceil\log_2p\rceil\) without worsening the other coordinate. The statistical rung remains restricted to a global optimizer, fixed \(p\), pointwise parameters outside the stated algebraic exceptional set, and simultaneous inference over a finite recovered component.
body.honest_scope: Population equivalence allows zero coefficients and all positive innovation variances and makes no faithfulness assumption. The bounded separator, exact sharp dictionary count, complete equivalence, and finite component enumeration hold for all \(p\) in the singleton-permitting target-local blocked class. No Pareto optimality of the two-block or height guarantees is claimed. Statistical conclusions are global-optimizer, fixed-\(p\), pointwise, and generic. Greedy GECS consistency, growing dimension, uniform inference near model intersections, cross-target edge-colour classes, constrained innovation variances, and cyclic graphs are outside scope.
